name: Scotts Turf Builder Lawn Food
use: Everyday fall feeding for the September and October applications. Widely stocked at Home Depot, Lowe's, Walmart and hardware stores.
rate: 1 lb N/1,000 sq ft ≈ 2.6 lb of product per 1,000 sq ft. The bag's "Turf Builder" setting delivers ≈1.2 lb N/1,000.
cautions: Reformulated in April 2026 from 32-0-4 to 38-0-4. Older 32-0-4 bags (5,000 / 15,000 sq ft) are still on some shelves, so set the calculator to the analysis on your bag.
Apply when temperatures are 60–90°F, not right before heavy rain; sweep granules off pavement.

name: Scotts Turf Builder WinterGuard Fall Lawn Food
use: A retail "winterizer" for the November feeding. The potassium doesn't hurt, but it's nitrogen that drives spring green-up.
rate: One application Aug–Nov; bag rate ≈0.8–0.9 lb N/1,000. For a full 1 lb N, use ≈3.1 lb per 1,000 sq ft.

package.label: 10 lb (4,000 sq ft) or 32.3 lb (12,000 sq ft)

cautions: Keep granules off driveways and sidewalks (sweep back onto the lawn).

name: LESCO 28-0-12 50% PolyPlus (50 lb)
use: Pro-grade fall fertilizer with 50% slow-release nitrogen and iron. The cheapest per pound of N for bigger lawns.
rate: 3.57 lb per 1,000 sq ft = 1 lb N; one 50 lb bag covers up to 14,000 sq ft.

package.label: 50 lb (up to 14,000 sq ft at 1 lb N)

where: SiteOne Landscape Supply (call the branch; sometimes "available by request")
cautions: Water in, and sweep granules off paving (iron can stain concrete).

name: Urea 46-0-0 (e.g., LESCO 46-0-0 Urea)
use: The classic, cheap November "winterizer": all quick-release nitrogen, taken up by roots for an early spring green-up (K-State).
rate: 2.2 lb per 1,000 sq ft = 1 lb N; never more than 1 lb N at once. A 50 lb bag covers up to 23,000 sq ft.
where: SiteOne (ask whether your branch sells to homeowners), farm co-ops
cautions: Quick-release: water in with about ¼ in (or apply right before rain) to prevent burn and nitrogen loss.
Not for spring or summer use on a rain-fed lawn.

name: Milorganite
use: Slow-release, non-burning organic nitrogen: forgiving for beginners, and a safe choice for the optional light April feeding.
rate: Bag rate: 32 lb per 2,500 sq ft (≈0.77 lb N/1,000). For 1 lb N use ≈16.7 lb per 1,000 sq ft.

package.label: 32 lb (2,500 sq ft at bag rate)

where: Home Depot, Lowe's, Ace, garden centers
cautions: Made from Milwaukee wastewater biosolids. Some dogs love the smell and will roll in or eat it; sweep it off hard surfaces.
Low analysis means many bags for a full feeding; cost per pound of N is high.

name: Scotts Turf Builder Starter Food for New Grass
use: High-phosphorus starter fertilizer applied at seeding. Phosphorus helps new roots; established lawns rarely need it.
rate: Bag rate: 15 lb per 5,000 sq ft (≈0.7 lb N/1,000). Apply the day you seed.
cautions: Keep away from storm drains; don't apply before heavy rain. Keep soil moist until seedlings are 2 in tall.

name: Scotts Turf Builder Triple Action Built For Seeding
use: Starter fertilizer plus a seed-safe weed preventer in one bag. Blocks crabgrass and dandelion seedlings for about 6 weeks while new grass comes up. It's the easy retail version of "Tenacity at seeding."
rate: Bag rate: 17.2 lb per 4,000 sq ft, applied at seeding.
cautions: Doesn't kill existing weeds, and contains no seed.
Not for bentgrass, bermuda, zoysia or St. Augustine lawns. Keep out of vegetable beds.
Replaced the discontinued "Starter Food for New Grass Plus Weed Preventer."

name: Espoma Garden-tone
use: Organic vegetable-garden fertilizer with microbes; work it in before planting and side-dress midseason.
rate: Soil prep: 3 lb per 50 sq ft (the label rate). Side-dress per label.
where: Garden centers, Home Depot, Lowe's, Ace
cautions: Keep it off stems and leaves.

name: Espoma Tomato-tone
use: Organic tomato and pepper food: a handful in the planting hole, then side-dress when fruit sets.
rate: 3 Tbsp per plant at planting (label), or 3 lb per 50 sq ft for beds.
where: Garden centers, Home Depot, Lowe's, Ace
cautions: Keep at least 3 in from stems; water in. The added calcium won't fix blossom-end rot caused by uneven watering.

name: Balanced fertilizer 10-10-10 (any brand)
use: MU's default pre-plant vegetable fertilizer when you don't have a soil test; also for garlic at planting.
rate: About 3 lb per 100 sq ft worked into the top few inches before planting (MU default without a soil test).
where: Farm & garden stores, Tractor Supply, Home Depot, Lowe's
cautions: Many established gardens already test high in phosphorus. A soil test tells you whether you need the middle number at all.

name: Pelletized agricultural lime
use: Raises soil pH, but only when an MU soil test says your lawn is at pH 5.8 or lower.
rate: Your soil report's rate, but no more than 50 lb per 1,000 sq ft per application (MU); split bigger rates about 6 months apart; fall or early winter is best.
cautions: Never lime "just because." Many KC soils don't need it, and over-liming is hard to undo.

name: Compost (Missouri Organic Recycling or your own pile)
use: The fix for KC clay. Work 2–3 in into garden beds, topdress ¼ in on the lawn after aerating, and fill raised beds with a topsoil–compost blend.
rate: Beds: 2–3 in worked in. Lawn: ¼ in after core aeration (keep at least ¾ of the grass blades showing). See the mulch & compost calculator.

package.label: Bulk by the cubic yard (delivery available) or bagged

where: Missouri Organic Recycling: four KC-metro yards, plus delivery
cautions: Never add sand to clay; it makes a concrete-like mix. Compost is the amendment.

name: Soil Service "KC Endurance" tall fescue
use: A local blend chosen for the KC transition zone (the store says from NTEP and TWCA data). Pick it if you want straight fescue.
rate: Overseed 4–5 lb/1,000 sq ft; bare soil 7–9 lb/1,000 (MU).

package.label: By the pound or bag. Ask for the current tag.

where: Soil Service Garden Center, 7130 Troost Ave, KC MO · (816) 444-3403
cautions: Cultivar picks are the seller's claims. Read the tag and compare the names to NTEP data (Lawn guide).

name: Soil Service "KC Marathon" (fescue + 10% bluegrass)
analysis: KC Endurance + 10% Kentucky bluegrass by weight
use: Our top pick for a rain-fed KC lawn: the 90/10 tall fescue–bluegrass recipe, locally blended. The bluegrass fills small gaps.
rate: Overseed 4–5 lb/1,000 sq ft; bare soil 7–9 lb/1,000.

package.label: By the pound or bag. Ask for the current tag.

where: Soil Service Garden Center, 7130 Troost Ave, KC MO · (816) 444-3403
cautions: Kentucky bluegrass needs 2–3 weeks to germinate, versus about 1 week for fescue. Keep the seedbed moist longer.

name: Grass Pad Heat Wave® Fescue / Heat Wave® Plus
analysis: Turf-type tall fescue blend; "Plus" = 95% Heat Wave + 5% Blue Wave bluegrass
use: KC-area store blend from Grass Pad. Heat Wave Plus adds a little bluegrass.
rate: Grass Pad says: overseed 5–8, bare ground 10–12, dormant seeding 8–10 lb/1,000 sq ft (higher than MU's 7–9).
where: Grass Pad stores in Olathe, Lee's Summit, Kansas City (Barry Rd), Bonner Springs and Stilwell
cautions: Seller's blend. Check the tag for cultivar names and a recent test date.

name: LESCO Kansas Excalibur Blend (or LESCO Tuf Turf 90/10)
analysis: 100% tall fescue, 3 varieties, blue-tag certified (Tuf Turf Mix: 90% tall fescue / 10% bluegrass)
use: Certified, weed-free contractor seed at a good price per pound for big lawns.
rate: SiteOne lists 6–8 lb/1,000 for new seedings; overseed about half that.
cautions: Blue tag = certified varieties, but still read the tag for the test date.

name: Jonathan Green Black Beauty Ultra
analysis: ≈80% tall fescue (3 cultivars) + 10% Kentucky bluegrass + 10% perennial ryegrass
use: The best widely stocked national mix: mostly turf-type fescue with some bluegrass. The ryegrass sprouts fast but may thin out in a KC summer.
rate: 25 lb covers 5,000 sq ft new or 10,000 sq ft overseeded (label).
cautions: Contains about 10% perennial ryegrass, so look for tags that keep it at 10% or less.

name: Pennington The Rebels Tall Fescue Grass Seed Blend
use: Big-box option for straight turf-type tall fescue. Add ~10% bluegrass yourself if you want the 90/10 recipe.
rate: New lawn 8–10 lb/1,000; overseed 4–6 lb/1,000 (label).
cautions: Don't grab Pennington Kentucky 31 by mistake; that's a forage type.

name: Mix-your-own blend from NTEP-proven cultivars
analysis: e.g., equal parts of 3 tall fescues + ~10% bluegrass
use: For the enthusiast: buy 2–3 single-cultivar tall fescues that did well at the non-irrigated Manhattan, KS NTEP site (Titan GLX, Xanadu, Hellcat GLR, Triad) or across the transition zone (Spyder 2LS, Titanium G-LS, Daybreak), and mix them (MU IPM suggests equal parts).
rate: Same rates as any tall fescue. The seed calculator has a mix-your-own helper.
where: SiteOne, independent seed stores (ask), online seed sellers
cautions: Cultivar availability changes yearly; NTEP data and the Turfgrass Trial Explorer (Library) are your guide.

name: Merriam Feed + Seed "Revolution" fescue / "Tri-Star" blend
analysis: Store blends (contents not published; ask for the tag)
use: Local feed-store seed sold by the pound, handy if you only need a little for patching.
rate: Standard tall fescue rates.
where: Merriam Feed + Seed, 9309 Johnson Dr, Merriam KS
cautions: We couldn't verify what's in these blends, so read the tag before buying.

name: Kentucky 31 tall fescue (AVOID for lawns)
use: Listed so you recognize it: cheap and tough, but coarse, clumpy and pale. MU says forage types belong on roadsides. In NTEP's 2018 test it scored 4.4, versus 6.3–6.4 for the best turf types.
rate: If used anyway: 10 lb/1,000 sq ft (MU).
cautions: Its endophyte is toxic to horses and cattle.
Buy a turf-type blend instead.

name: Hi-Yield Turf & Ornamental Weed & Grass Stopper with Dimension
use: Our pick for a homeowner crabgrass preventer. Dithiopyr gives season-long prevention and also kills crabgrass up to about 4 weeks after it emerges, so a late application still works.
rate: 2.4 lb per 1,000 sq ft (2–3 months) up to 3.2 lb (3–4 months); 9.6 lb bag ≈ 4,000 sq ft. Water in with ¼ in.
where: Independent garden centers & farm stores (Hi-Yield/Ferti-lome dealers), Amazon
cautions: No reseeding for 10 weeks after a spring application (16 weeks after a split program). Don't use where you'll seed this spring.
On new tall fescue seedings the label allows application 2 weeks after first germination. Read it first.

name: LESCO Stonewall 0.43% 0-0-7 (prodiamine granular)
use: Granular prodiamine: the longest-lasting crabgrass preventer, one application at redbud bloom. Cheap per 1,000 sq ft for larger lawns.
rate: 3.44 lb per 1,000 sq ft; 50 lb covers up to 14,535 sq ft. Water in.
cautions: Doesn't kill crabgrass that's already up.
Prodiamine blocks grass seed for months: plan on no seeding in treated areas until fall (label intervals are about 4–6 months depending on rate).

name: Barricade 4FL
use: Sprayable prodiamine for pump-sprayer users: very cheap per application, one spray in spring.
rate: Label annual maximum for tall fescue: 0.5–1.1 fl oz per 1,000 sq ft. Use the spray-mix calculator; water in.
cautions: Label wait before overseeding: 16 fl oz/acre → 4 months; 21 fl oz/acre → 4–5 months; 24 fl oz/acre → 5–6 months.
On new seedings, wait 60 days or until after the 2nd mowing, whichever is longer.

name: Prodiamine 65 WDG (generic Barricade)
use: Generic sprayable prodiamine; one 5 lb jug lasts a homeowner many years.
rate: Tall fescue annual maximum: 0.36–0.83 oz per 1,000 sq ft (label). Weigh it on a kitchen scale.
cautions: Overseeding delay of 4–6 months depending on rate.
Keep the powder away from kids and pets; label PPE applies.

name: Dimension 2EW
use: Sprayable dithiopyr: season-long prevention plus early post-emergent kill of young crabgrass.
rate: Up to 0.73 fl oz per 1,000 sq ft per application, 2.2 fl oz per year (label).
cautions: Reseeding within 3 months of an application may fail (4 months after a heavier split program).

name: Tenacity
use: The seed-safe weed preventer: spray at seeding to block crabgrass and broadleaf seedlings (K-State). Later it works as a post-emergent on young crabgrass, nimblewill and some broadleaves.
rate: Tall fescue: 5–8 fl oz/acre ≈ 0.115–0.184 fl oz (about 3.4–5.4 mL, roughly ¾–1 tsp) per 1,000 sq ft. At seeding, **no** surfactant; post-emergent use adds a non-ionic surfactant and repeats in 2–3 weeks.
cautions: Not for seed mixes with more than 20% fine fescue by weight.
**No vegetables or other non-turf crops in treated soil for 18 months.** Keep it far from the garden.
Weeds (and sometimes turf) turn white for a couple of weeks; that's normal.
On new grass, wait 4 weeks or 2 mowings after emergence before a post-emergent spray (Purdue).

name: Preen Garden Weed Preventer
use: Stops weed seeds from sprouting in established flower beds for 8–12 weeks. Apply after spring cleanup and mulching.
rate: About 1 oz per 10 sq ft (5.6 lb covers 900 sq ft); water in lightly.

package.label: 5.6 lb (900 sq ft) to 31 lb (5,000 sq ft)

where: Home Depot, Lowe's, Walmart, garden centers
cautions: Not for lawns. Don't use where you're sowing flower seeds; it's fine around plants that are 2–3 in tall.

name: Preen Natural Vegetable Garden Weed Preventer
use: Food-safe weed preventer for the vegetable garden, around transplants and established seedlings. Lasts 4–6 weeks.
rate: 5 lb covers 250 sq ft.
cautions: Also stops vegetable seeds: use only after seedlings have true leaves (2–3 in).
Don't water for 2–3 days after the first watering-in.

name: SpeedZone EW Lawn Weed Killer
use: Fast, broad-spectrum broadleaf killer (dandelion, clover, henbit, chickweed, plantain and more) that works in cooler fall and spring weather.
rate: Cool-season lawns: 1.1–1.8 fl oz per 1,000 sq ft (label).
cautions: Max 2 broadcast applications a year, 30 days apart; not above 90°F.
New seedings: wait until after the 2nd mowing (label). This plan uses 3 mowings, following K-State MF736.
Drift kills tomatoes, grapes and redbuds. Spray on calm days, away from gardens.

name: Ortho Weed B Gon Chickweed, Clover & Oxalis Killer for Lawns
use: The best retail choice for tough weeds: ground ivy (creeping Charlie), wild violet, clover, chickweed and oxalis. Best in fall.
rate: Concentrate: 1 fl oz per gallon per 200 sq ft (16 oz treats 3,200 sq ft).
cautions: Not for bermuda or zoysia lawns. Never on or near fruits, vegetables or flowers. Apply below 90°F.

name: Ortho Weed B-gon Lawn Weed Killer + Crabgrass Control
use: Kills crabgrass that got through (quinclorac) plus common broadleaf weeds. Spot-spray young crabgrass in June–July.
rate: 32 fl oz concentrate treats 5,000 sq ft (label).
cautions: Max 2 applications a year, 21+ days apart, at 45–90°F. Don't use treated clippings as garden mulch.
Renamed from "Weed B Gon Plus Crabgrass Control."

name: Drive XLR8
use: Pro crabgrass killer that also hits clover. Safe on tall fescue, even at seeding.
rate: 1.45 fl oz per 1,000 sq ft plus methylated seed oil 0.55 fl oz/1,000; max 2.9 fl oz/1,000 per year.
cautions: **No tomatoes or carrots for 24 months (eggplant 12 months) in treated soil.** Tomatoes are extremely sensitive; keep it away from the garden.

name: SedgeHammer / SedgeHammer+
activeIngredient: Halosulfuron-methyl (75% powder; SedgeHammer+ 5% with built-in surfactant)
use: The go-to for yellow nutsedge in lawns. Spray young plants in late May–June.
rate: SedgeHammer+: one 13.5 g pouch per gallon per 1,000 sq ft. A second application 6–10 weeks later if needed.
cautions: Don't mow 2 days before or after; needs 4 rain-free hours.

name: Ortho Nutsedge Killer for Lawns (Ready-To-Spray)
use: Big-box nutsedge option; hose-end sprayer.
rate: 32 fl oz covers 5,000 sq ft; best on sedge under 3 in tall.
cautions: Established turf only; not over flowers or vegetables.

name: 41% glyphosate concentrate (Compare-N-Save or Hi-Yield Killzall)
use: Spot-kills bermudagrass, zoysia and nimblewill patches before fall seeding; also for cut-stump treatment of bush honeysuckle.
rate: Mix per label for perennial grasses; spray patches in August and again about a month later, then seed after 7 days (MU).

package.label: 32 oz (makes up to 21 gal), 1 gal, 2.5 gal

cautions: Non-selective: kills any green plant it touches, including your lawn. Use a shield or a dedicated sprayer on a calm day.
Many consumer "Roundup" products no longer contain glyphosate (or only a little). Read the active ingredient on the label, not the brand.

name: Ortho Grass B Gon Garden Grass Killer
use: Kills bermudagrass and other grasses creeping into flower beds and shrubs without hurting broadleaf ornamentals.
rate: Ready-to-spray; repeat per label for bermudagrass.
cautions: Not for lawns (it kills lawn grass). The label covers ornamentals only, with **no vegetables**.

name: Scotts GrubEx1 Season Long Grub Killer
use: Preventive grub control, only if grubs damaged your lawn last year. Chlorantraniliprole is much easier on bees than older grub products.
rate: 14.35 lb covers 5,000 sq ft; apply in May (K-State) and water in.
cautions: Keep out of flower beds, vegetable gardens and water.

name: BioAdvanced Season Long Grub Control Plus Turf Revitalizer
use: Alternative grub preventer, May through June (K-State).
rate: 12 lb covers 5,000 sq ft; water in within 24 hours.
cautions: Imidacloprid is highly toxic to bees. **Mow off flowering clover and dandelions first**, and never apply to blooming plants.
Not in vegetable gardens; not on linden or basswood.

name: BioAdvanced 24 Hour Grub Killer Plus Granules
use: The rescue product: kills grubs that are actively damaging the lawn (late July–September) when you find 5–10 or more per sq ft.
rate: 10 lb covers 5,000 sq ft; water in with about ½ in within 24 hours.
cautions: Organophosphate. Keep kids and pets off until it's watered in and dry. Use only when grubs are confirmed.

name: Bt caterpillar spray (Monterey B.t., Safer Caterpillar Killer II, Bonide Thuricide)
use: Kills only caterpillars that eat treated leaves: cabbageworms, hornworms, bagworms (while bags are small) and sod webworms. Safe for bees and people.
rate: Monterey: 1–1.5 Tbsp per gallon; Thuricide ½–4 tsp per gallon; repeat every 5–7 days while caterpillars feed.
where: Garden centers, Home Depot, Lowe's, Amazon
cautions: Works best on young caterpillars; sunlight breaks it down in a few days.

name: Monterey Garden Insect Spray (spinosad)
use: Organic option for Colorado potato beetle larvae, caterpillars, thrips, leafminers and bagworms.
rate: 2 fl oz (4 Tbsp) per gallon.
cautions: Toxic to bees for about 3 hours after spraying: spray in the evening and not on open flowers.

name: Bonide Eight Insect Control (Vegetable, Fruit & Flower)
use: Labeled for squash bugs and cucumber beetles on squash and other cucurbits (0-day harvest interval).
rate: Cucurbits: 2 fl oz per gallon; up to 8 applications per season (label).
cautions: Highly toxic to bees: spray late in the day, never on open flowers.
Its label does **not** list squash vine borer. For borers, use an insecticide whose label lists them, or use row cover and trap crops.

name: Insecticidal soap (e.g., Safer Brand Insect Killing Soap)
use: Aphids, spider mites and whiteflies on vegetables and flowers. Kills on contact, no residue.
rate: Per label; must hit the insects directly (undersides of leaves).
cautions: Can burn leaves in hot sun; spray in the morning or evening. Test a leaf first on sensitive plants.

name: BioAdvanced 12 Month Tree & Shrub Protect & Feed II
use: DIY emerald ash borer protection for ash trees under about 20 in diameter, poured as a soil drench each spring around pear/crabapple bloom (Missouri homeowner EAB guide). Also for bagworm-free evergreens.
rate: 1 fl oz per inch of trunk circumference, in a bucket of water poured at the trunk base (label).
cautions: Highly toxic to bees: never on flowering plants (ash is wind-pollinated, so it's OK). Not on linden or basswood; fruit and nut trees only if not bearing.
Trees over 20 in need a professional trunk injection.

name: Scotts DiseaseEx Lawn Fungicide
use: Preventive brown patch control, only for lawns that get hit hard every summer. Most fescue recovers in fall without it.
rate: Preventive: 2 lb per 1,000 sq ft (10 lb covers 5,000 sq ft); repeat at 14–28 days per label from late June.
cautions: Toxic to fish; keep out of storm drains. Rotate with a different fungicide group if you spray repeatedly.

name: BioAdvanced Fungus Control for Lawns
use: Alternative brown patch product, from a different chemical group than azoxystrobin, so you can alternate them.
rate: Ready-to-spray: 32 fl oz covers 5,000 sq ft. Granules: 2 lb per 1,000 sq ft.
cautions: Keep people and pets off until dry. Toxic to fish.

name: GardenTech Daconil Fungicide Concentrate
use: Protects tomatoes from early blight and Septoria leaf spot when the disease is severe. Spray every 7–10 days per label.
rate: Per label for tomatoes; observe the listed days-to-harvest.
cautions: Its label says **do not use on home lawns**. Eye irritant: wear eye protection.

name: Bonide Captain Jack's Liquid Copper Fungicide
use: Organic-approved protectant for tomato blights and leaf spots; OK up to the day of harvest.
rate: Per label; repeat every 7–10 days in wet weather.
cautions: Protectant only: it can't cure infected leaves. Some roses are copper-sensitive.

name: Agribon+ AG-19 row cover
use: Frost insurance (2–4°F of protection) in spring and fall, plus a physical barrier against squash vine borers, cucumber beetles, cabbageworms and flea beetles until crops bloom.
rate: Drape over wire hoops; bury or pin the edges.
where: Johnny's Selected Seeds, garden centers, Amazon
cautions: Remove from squash and cucumbers when they flower so bees can pollinate.

name: Texas Tomato Cage (or a DIY concrete-wire cage)
use: Six-foot heavy-duty cages that hold big indeterminate tomatoes all season. The flimsy cone cages collapse by July.
rate: One per plant; push legs 1.5–2 ft into the ground.

package.label: Large 24 in or medium 20 in diameter, 6 ft tall

where: Amazon, some garden centers. DIY: 6×6-in concrete reinforcing wire from a home center.
cautions: Anchor with a stake in open, windy yards.

name: Soaker hose or drip-irrigation kit
brand: Rain Bird, Orbit, Snip-n-Drip and others
use: Waters beds and vegetables at the roots without a sprinkler system. Lay it under the mulch and put it on a hose timer.
rate: About 1 in of water per week total (rain + watering); run long enough to wet the top 6 in.
cautions: Use a pressure regulator with drip kits; drain and store before the first hard freeze.

name: Wheat straw (garden mulch)
use: Mulch for vegetables and over fall garlic. It holds even moisture (the real fix for blossom-end rot) and keeps soil splash off tomato leaves.
rate: 2–3 in once soil has warmed (late May); 3–4 in over garlic after the ground cools.
cautions: Straw, not hay: hay is full of weed seeds.

name: Shredded hardwood mulch
use: Bed mulch that holds moisture on clay, blocks weeds and breaks down into soil.
rate: 2–3 in deep, pulled 2–3 in back from stems and trunks.

package.label: 2 cu ft bags or bulk by the yard

where: Missouri Organic (bulk), home centers, garden centers
cautions: No mulch volcanoes against trunks.

name: Seed-starting setup: LED shop light, heat mat, seed-starting mix, outlet timer
use: Starts onions (January), broccoli and cabbage (February), peppers (early March) and tomatoes (mid-March) indoors.
rate: Light 2–3 in above seedlings, 14–16 hours a day; heat mat 75–85°F until sprouted.
where: Home Depot, Lowe's, garden centers, Amazon
cautions: Use seed-starting mix, not garden soil.

name: Hose faucet timer (Orbit 62061N or Melnor AquaTimer)
use: The single best-value tool for a no-sprinkler-system yard. It waters new seed 2–3 times a day while you're at work and runs early-morning drought soaks.
rate: New seed: 3 short cycles a day. Drought soak: two runs 30 minutes apart, 4–10 a.m.
cautions: Bring it inside before freezing weather.

name: Melnor Turbo Oscillating Sprinkler (XT4200, 4,500 sq ft)
use: Even, rectangular coverage for germinating seed and survival soaks.
rate: Do the tuna-can test to learn its inches per hour.

name: Stratus Precision Rain Gauge (4-inch, CoCoRaHS-approved)
use: Know exactly how much rain fell in your yard: summer storms vary a lot block to block. Log readings here to sharpen the drought alerts, and share them with CoCoRaHS.
rate: Read at the same time each morning.
cautions: Mount it clear of roofs and trees, and bring the inner tube in before freezes.

name: Soil thermometer (5-in dial probe)
use: Checks the cues this plan uses: crabgrass (~55°F), tomatoes (60°F+), peppers and melons (65°F+), garlic and bulbs (below 60°F).
rate: Measure at 2 in deep, mid-morning, for several days.

name: Soil sampling probe (12-in)
use: Pulls clean soil-test cores in seconds and shows how deep moisture and roots go.
rate: 10–15 cores per sample.

name: MU soil test (regular fertility)
use: The best $15 you'll spend: tells you exactly what lime and fertilizer your lawn and garden need, or don't need.
rate: Every 2–3 years; separate samples for lawn, garden and beds.

package.label: About 1½ cups of dry soil per sample

where: Your county MU Extension office (call ahead), or mail to the MU lab

name: Broadcast spreader (Scotts EdgeGuard DLX or EarthWay 2150)
use: Even fertilizer, seed and granular pre-emergent. The EdgeGuard DLX is fine for typical lawns; the EarthWay 2150 is a commercial-grade step up.
rate: Set to half the label setting and make two passes at right angles.

package.label: EdgeGuard DLX: up to 15,000 sq ft per fill

where: Home Depot, Lowe's; EarthWay from SiteOne or online

name: 1–2 gallon pump sprayer (keep one for weed killer only)
use: For spot-spraying weeds, Tenacity and liquid pre-emergents.
rate: Calibrate: time how long it takes to spray 1,000 sq ft evenly with plain water.
cautions: Label it "HERBICIDE" and never use it on vegetables.

name: Core aerator rental (or hire it done)
brand: Home Depot / Lowe's tool rental, rental yards
use: Pulls cores from compacted clay so seed, water and air reach the roots. Do it right before overseeding in September, with 2 passes.
rate: Soil should be moist but not sticky (after a ½-in rain or watering).
where: Home Depot/Lowe's tool rental, local rental yards, lawn services
cautions: Heavy (~200 lb): bring a helper and a truck. Mark sprinkler heads, invisible-fence wires and shallow cables first; call 811 if you're unsure.

name: Mower blade sharpening (or a spare blade)
use: Sharp blades cut cleanly; dull blades shred tips and invite disease. Sharpen in spring and again in early summer.
rate: About every 25 hours of mowing.
cautions: Disconnect the spark plug before removing a blade.

name: Rain barrel with downspout diverter
use: Free water for beds and containers. Missouri law protects your right to collect rainwater, even inside city limits (RSMo 640.648).
rate: A 1,000 sq ft roof sheds about 600 gallons per inch of rain.
cautions: Screen it and use Mosquito Dunks. Drain and disconnect before hard freezes. Use on ornamentals; wash any produce well.

name: Victor Out O'Sight or Wire Tek EasySet mole trap
use: Trapping is the only reliable mole control. Grub killers don't get rid of moles, which mostly eat earthworms.
rate: Set on an active runway: flatten a section of tunnel, and wherever it's pushed back up within a day, set the trap there.
cautions: Set the safety catch while installing; keep kids and pets away.

name: 24-in rabbit fence (1-in mesh chicken wire or welded wire)
use: Keeps rabbits off beans, lettuce, peas and young transplants. Put it up in early April.
rate: 24 in tall, bottom buried 3–6 in or pinned flat outward.

name: ¼-inch hardware cloth (trunk guards)
use: Winter trunk guards against rabbits and voles on young trees and shrubs.
rate: 18–24 in tall cylinders, 1–2 in away from the trunk; remove in spring.

name: Liquid Fence Deer & Rabbit Repellent
use: Scent/taste repellent for hostas, tulips, daylilies and other deer and rabbit favorites.
rate: Spray weekly for 3 weeks, then monthly and after heavy rain.
cautions: Smells bad until dry. Only tall fencing (7–8 ft) fully stops deer.

name: Sawyer Permethrin Fabric Treatment
use: Treat your yard clothes and shoes against ticks and chiggers, which are both abundant in Missouri. Lasts 6 weeks or 6 washes.
rate: About 4.5 oz per outfit; spray outdoors and let dry.
cautions: Clothing only, never skin. **Toxic to cats until dry.** Use DEET or picaridin on skin.

name: Summit Mosquito Dunks
use: Kills mosquito larvae in rain barrels, birdbaths and water that can't be dumped. Harmless to pets, birds and fish.
rate: 1 dunk per 100 sq ft of water surface; lasts 30+ days.
